analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change. I examined the changed hunks: the date bump, the new paragraph at lines 3528-3536, and the cluster runtime facts rewording near line 5230. That last hunk lies outside the supplied excerpts, so I could not review it in full.

The new paragraph describes where the cluster service heartbeat is written (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE; service-health.json vs part-health.json). The supervisor's liveness guard accepts only a beat carrying the service's own PID, and a coordinator-paired part writes to a separate file so it cannot overwrite that heartbeat. If this matches the code, it is a hardening and availability property, not a regression. Nothing in it touches the coordinator-to-provider trust boundary (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), prefix-cache storage (T-041) or fan control (TB-010). The prose also introduces no new attack surface.

Remaining questions need the code, which was not supplied. First, whether ClusterService.partEnvironment and ClusterServiceAgent.healthPath really enforce the PID check and file separation as documented. Second, whether the health files are owner-only. Third, whether the signed-release computation of cluster_runtime approval digests, mentioned in the hunk near line 5230, preserves admission integrity; it appears to move digest registration from guided setup into the release lane, which a deeper pass on the platform and release side should confirm. The excerpts of the 3231-3998 range are unchanged context: Flint, tensor-parallel, link probe and share probe documentation.

I claim no code-level conclusions beyond the documented text.
